Daily Brief

The International Court of Justice delivered a historic verdict Thursday, ruling for the first time that a state—Myanmar—committed genocide, finding the country responsible for atrocities against its Rohingya minority during the 2017 military crackdown [RFI, BBC, Al Jazeera, The Hindu]. The ruling came as Presidents Trump, Xi, and Putin concluded unprecedented trilateral talks in Shenzhen on the APEC sidelines, issuing a joint statement on nuclear risk reduction and energy supplies while notably omitting any reference to the Ukraine war [ABC Australia, Nikkei Asia, BBC]. European leaders were conspicuously absent from these discussions despite their far-reaching implications [RFI]. In financial markets, AI firm Anthropic shattered records with its $1.5 trillion Nasdaq debut, raising $81 billion in the largest IPO ever [France 24, BBC]. Meanwhile, the EU delayed new methane emissions rules until 2029 amid energy market pressures [RFI], and Putin warned of a 'far more painful' response to Ukraine's continued strikes on the Crimean Bridge [BBC]. Five EU nations also announced plans for offshore immigration return centers in Rwanda [The Guardian].

01 Geopolitics

ICJ Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya in Historic First Verdict

  • The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in northern Rakhine State, marking the first time in the court's 80-year history it has found a state responsible for genocide
  • The court ordered Myanmar to provide safe passage for refugees to return home and to pay compensation to victims
  • Nine of 15 judges voted in favor of the genocide finding after seven years of deliberations on the case brought by Gambia in 2019
  • Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar, the world's largest refugee camp, watched the verdict on giant screens, with many breaking down in tears

02 Geopolitics

Trump, Xi, and Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in Shenzhen, Exclude Europe

  • US President Trump, Chinese President Xi, and Russian President Putin met for approximately 90 minutes in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit—the first trilateral meeting of these three leaders
  • The joint statement addressed nuclear risk reduction, energy supplies, and reform of the UN, but made no mention of the war in Ukraine despite pre-summit expectations
  • The declaration included an agreement that the International Criminal Court and similar bodies should not abuse their jurisdiction
  • European Union representatives were notably absent from discussions that could have significant implications for the continent

Anthropic Begins Trading at $1.5 Trillion Valuation in Largest IPO on Record

  • AI company Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the proposed $70-$78 range, valuing the company at approximately $1.5 trillion
  • The offering raised $81 billion, surpassing SpaceX's June listing as the largest initial public offering ever
  • Shares began trading on Nasdaq under ticker 'ANT,' with the tech-heavy index rising nearly 2% at market open
  • CEO Dario Amodei said the debut strengthens the company's financial position and its commitment to responsible AI development

04 Conflict

Putin Threatens 'Far More Painful' Retaliation After Ukraine's Crimean Bridge Strikes

  • The Crimean Bridge was struck for a third time this week early Thursday, following a Tuesday attack that destroyed the central road section and collapsed part into the water
  • Russian President Putin vowed Moscow's response would be 'far more painful' than Kyiv's strikes, claiming the bridge was used exclusively for civilian purposes
  • Ukraine's defence ministry stated the strikes represent 'time gained and lives saved' by reducing supplies reaching Russian forces
  • The collapse represents the worst damage to the strategically important structure in several years

05 Climate

EU Delays Methane Emissions Rules Until 2029 Amid Energy Market Pressures

  • The European Union agreed to postpone new methane reporting requirements for oil, gas, and coal importers from January 2027 to January 2029
  • The compromise came after overnight negotiations, with the European Commission and member states favoring a one-year delay while Parliament sought three years
  • The decision follows energy supply uncertainties driven by the Middle East war and international market disruptions
  • Environmental groups warned the delay risks undermining EU climate ambitions on methane, the second-largest contributor to global warming
